stdio_review.algorithm_assessment: Any two monotone full paths have total balance zero. Swapping the order of a right/down move within one square therefore forces its upper-right and lower-left entries to match; consequently each anti-diagonal is constant. Conversely any Dyck word on the n+m-1 anti-diagonals gives a valid array, since every monotone path reads exactly that word. The first differing cell between two arrays is determined by the minimum priority in the first differing anti-diagonal under priority ordering. Unrank Dyck words in that induced order: tentatively assign an opening parenthesis and count completions with an exact nonnegative-balance DP respecting every fixed position. Choose the closing branch only after subtracting the entire opening-branch count. Python integers preserve exact ranking up to 10^18 and beyond; no arbitrary tie choice or non-unique output is involved.
stdio_review.limitations: One source reviewer plus actual isolated tests, not independent dual semantic review.
